summary: Implemented the rich.progress file-reading feature without running any code. Changes (all additive, nothing committed): rich/progress.py gained private _ProgressReader and _ProgressContext classes, module-level open and wrap_file with overloads, a shared _create_file_progress helper, and Progress.open and Progress.wrap_file methods. tests/test_progress.py gained 19 new tests before the __main__ block. docs/source/progress.rst gained the two requested subsections under Advanced usage. CHANGELOG.md gained one Added entry linking PR 1759. Verification was by reading only: tests, black, isort and mypy have not been run, so the code is unverified at runtime. Known consequence of the specified ordering: Progress.open creates the task before opening the file, so a failure after the size lookup (e.g. permission error) leaves a task behind; a missing file is caught earlier and creates none.
